subproblem.title: Vertical first variation: the graph solves the prescribed-mean-curvature system (Step 4)
subproblem.statement:
Let n >= 1, U open in R^(n+l), V = v(M, theta) with generalized mean curvature H in U, h locally C^{q,alpha} in U (IsLocallyHolderCkα q alpha h U) with H = h mu_V-a.e. Let xi in R^(n+l), 0 < s <= R, the closed ball B_s(xi) contained in U, Q a linear isometry, u : R^n -> R^l C^1 on the open ball of radius R about 0 with u(0) = 0, Q(spt V - xi) cap (open B_R(0)) = graph of u over the open ball cap (open B_R(0)), and mu_V restricted to the open ball Bs of radius s about xi equal to H^n restricted to spt V cap Bs. Put O := Q(U - xi) and F(z) := Q h(xi + Q^{-1} z). Then O is open, F is locally C^{q,alpha} on O, and there is r in (0, R] such that (x, u(x)) lies in O for |x| < r and, with J(P) := sqrt(det(I_n + (

)_{a,b})) the area element of the graph, integral over the open ball of radius r of DJ(Du)[Dphi] dx = - integral over that ball of J(Du) <(0, phi), F(x, u(x))> dx for every C^1 compactly supported phi : R^n -> R^l with tsupport phi in the open ball of radius r.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 4 of the parent-supplied proof (Simon, Ch. 5, proof of Theorem 7.1, p. 128, system (2), and Section 1, 1.1-1.3: the graph satisfies the Euler-Lagrange system of the area functional, with right-hand side coming from the generalized mean curvature). The vertical test field X := chi (0, phi) of the parent (rotated back) is used; the identification of the varifold's tangent planes with those of the graph, implicit in the parent's 'mu = H^n on the graph', is the sibling dohr_graph_tangent_planes (step 3). Notation. mu := V.weight, M := V.carrier, theta := V.mult, Sigma := V.support = U cap spt mu, H^n := muHE[n]. Bo_r denotes open balls and B_r closed balls. T(y) := Q(y - xi) and A(z) := xi + Q^{-1} z = T^{-1}(z) are isometric bijections of R^(n+l), T(Bo_r(xi)) = Bo_r(0). O := T(U) = (fun y => Q (y - xi)) '' U and F(z) := Q(h(A z)). G(x) := (x, u(x)) = graphPoint x (u x); Gamma := G(Bo^n_R(0)). pi : R^(n+l) -> R^n is the projection onto the first n coordinates (linear, pi(G(x)) = x, pi(graphPoint v w) = v). For a linear P : R^n -> R^l let g(P) be the n x n matrix with entries g(P)_{ab} := delta_{ab} +

and J(P) := det(g(P))^{1/2} (this is exactly the inline expression Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (1 + Matrix.of fun a b => inner (P e_a) (P e_b))) in the statement). g(P) >= I, so det g(P) >= 1 and J is C-infinity on L(R^n, R^l); DJ(P) denotes its derivative. Hypotheses used: (iii) mu restricted to Bo_s(xi) equals H^n restricted to Sigma cap Bo_s(xi); the graph identity T(Sigma) cap Bo_R(0) = Gamma cap Bo_R(0); u C^1 on Bo^n_R(0) with u(0) = 0; 0 < s <= R; B_s(xi) contained in U; U open; generalized mean curvature H with H = h mu-a.e.; h locally C^{q,alpha} in U. Facts used. (Area) Area formula for the injective map G on compact subsets of Bo^n_R(0), where G is Lipschitz (simongmt Chapter02.injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn and the weighted forms in AreaDomain.lean, Mathlib normalization; the Jacobian there equals J(Du(x)) a.e.): integral over G(S) of k dH^n = integral over S of k(G(x)) J(Du(x)) dx for Borel S and k >= 0; the Bochner-integral version for integrable real k follows by splitting k into positive and negative parts. J(Du(x)) = normDet(DG(x)) because DG(x)^T DG(x) = g(Du(x)). (Iso) H^n(T(S)) = H^n(S) (Mathlib IsometryEquiv.hausdorffMeasure_image). (TP) Sibling dohr_graph_tangent_planes (its second conjunct: the a.e. identification of V.tangentProj with the projection onto the rotated graph tangent plane). (Jacobi) D det(g)[E] = det(g) trace(g^{-1} E). 1. O is open and F is locally C^{q,alpha} on O. T is a homeomorphism, so O = T(U) is open. A maps O onto U and is affine with linear part Q^{-1}, so F = Q o h o A is C^q on O by the chain rule. For every j and every z, D^j F(z) = Q o D^j h(A z) o (Q^{-1}, ..., Q^{-1}) (composition with the affine isomorphism A and the linear isometry Q, valid at every point), and composing a multilinear map with linear isometries in every slot and on the output preserves its operator norm; hence |D^q F(z) - D^q F(w)| = |D^q h(A z) - D^q h(A w)|. If K is a compact subset of O, A(K) is a compact subset of U, so by IsLocallyHolderCkα q alpha h U there is C with |D^q h(a) - D^q h(b)| <= C |a - b|^alpha on A(K); since |A z - A w| = |z - w|, |D^q F(z) - D^q F(w)| <= C |z - w|^alpha on K. This proves the first two conjuncts. 2. Choice of r. G is continuous on Bo^n_R(0) and G(0) = (0, u(0)) = 0. Choose r in (0, R] such that |G(x)| < s for all x in Bo^n_r(0). Then A(G(x)) lies in Bo_s(xi), contained in U, so G(x) = T(A(G(x))) is in O: this is the third conjunct. 3. Tangent planes of V on Bo_s(xi). For x in Bo^n_R(0) let tau_x := DG(x)(R^n) = {(v, Du(x) v)} (an n-plane, DG(x) is injective), and for y with T(y) = G(x) let P_y := Q^{-1}(tau_x) = Submodule.map Q.symm (LinearMap.range (fderiv G x)). By (TP), applied with the given 0 < s <= R, closed B_s(xi) contained in U, u C^1 on Bo^n_R(0) and the graph identity: for mu-a.e. y in Bo_s(xi), V.tangentProj y = p_{P_y} (orthogonal projection onto P_y) for every x in Bo^n_R(0) with T(y) = G(x). Moreover mu(Bo_s(xi) minus Sigma) = 0 (Bo_s(xi) is contained in U; Mathlib measure_compl_support), and for y in Sigma cap Bo_s(xi) such an x exists and is unique (T(y) is in T(Sigma) cap Bo_s(0), contained in Gamma cap Bo_R(0); x = pi(T y)). By hypothesis (iii), the same statements hold for H^n-a.e. y in Sigma cap Bo_s(xi). 4. The test field. Fix phi : R^n -> R^l, C^1, with compact support and tsupport phi contained in Bo^n_r(0). K_phi := G(tsupport phi) is compact and, by step 2, contained in Bo_s(0). Choose psi : R^(n+l) -> [0,1], C-infinity, with psi = 1 on a neighbourhood of K_phi and tsupport psi a compact subset of Bo_s(0) (smooth Urysohn lemma). Define Xt(z) := psi(z) graphPoint 0 (phi(pi z)) and X(y) := Q^{-1}(Xt(T y)). X is C^1 with compact support and tsupport X = A(tsupport Xt), contained in A(tsupport psi), contained in Bo_s(xi), contained in U. So X is admissible in V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H. 5. Divergence of X on the graph. Let x in Bo^n_R(0) with |G(x)| < s and y := A(G(x)). If x is in tsupport phi, then psi = 1 near G(x), so Xt(z) = (0, phi(pi z)) near G(x) and DXt(G(x)) = (0, Dphi(x) o pi). If x is not in tsupport phi, then phi o pi vanishes on a neighbourhood of G(x) (pi is continuous and pi(G(x)) = x), so Xt = 0 near G(x) and DXt(G(x)) = 0 = (0, Dphi(x) o pi) because Dphi(x) = 0. In both cases DX(y) = Q^{-1} o (0, Dphi(x) o pi) o Q, and with p_{P_y} = Q^{-1} o p_{tau_x} o Q we get trace(DX(y) o p_{P_y}) = trace(Bx o p_{tau_x}) with Bx := (0, Dphi(x) o pi). With the basis b_a := DG(x) e_a = (e_a, D_a u(x)) of tau_x, Gram matrix g := g(Du(x)) and inverse (g^{ab}), p_{tau_x}(w) = sum_{a,c} g^{ac} b_a, hence trace(Bx o p_{tau_x}) = sum_{a,c} g^{ac} = sum_{a,c} g^{ac} , since Bx b_a = (0, D_a phi(x)). On the other hand, by (Jacobi), for linear P and Psi: DJ(P)[Psi] = (1/2) J(P) trace(g(P)^{-1} Dg(P)[Psi]) with Dg(P)[Psi]_{ac} = +

, so by symmetry of g^{-1}, DJ(P)[Psi] = J(P) sum_{a,c} g^{ac}

. Therefore J(Du(x)) * trace(DX(y) o p_{P_y}) = DJ(Du(x))[Dphi(x)], and both sides vanish when x is not in tsupport phi. 6. Left side of the first variation. divM X(y) = trace(DX(y) o V.tangentProj y) vanishes for y outside tsupport X (DX(y) = 0 there), and tsupport X is contained in Bo_s(xi). The function V.divM X is not known to be measurable a priori; by step 3 it agrees mu-a.e. with the explicit representative k(y) := trace(DX(y) o p_{P_y}) for y in Sigma cap Bo_s(xi) (P_y built from x = pi(T y)) and k(y) := 0 elsewhere, which is Borel measurable (it is continuous on the Borel set Sigma cap Bo_s(xi), because y -> x = pi(T y), x -> DG(x) and the orthogonal projection onto the range of DG(x) depend continuously on y, and it is 0 elsewhere), bounded, and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport X; so integral of divM X dmu = integral of k dmu (integral_congr_ae), and the following computations are done with k. Using (iii), then (Iso), then (Area) on D_s := {x in Bo^n_R(0) : |G(x)| < s} (G(D_s) = Gamma cap Bo_s(0); the integrand is supported in the compact set tsupport phi, contained in Bo^n_r(0), contained in D_s, where G is Lipschitz), and finally step 5: integral of V.divM X dmu = integral of k dmu = integral over Sigma cap Bo_s(xi) of trace(DX(y) o p_{P_y}) dH^n(y) = integral over Gamma cap Bo_s(0) of trace(DX(A z) o p_{P_{A z}}) dH^n(z) = integral over D_s of DJ(Du(x))[Dphi(x)] dx = integral over ball 0 r of fderiv J (fderiv u x) (fderiv phi x) dx. 7. Right side. X is bounded with compact support in U and H is locally mu-integrable on U, so is mu-integrable, and = mu-a.e. By (iii), (Iso) and (Area) as in step 6: integral of dmu = integral over Sigma cap Bo_s(xi) of dH^n = integral over D_s of J(Du(x)) dx = integral over D_s of psi(G(x)) J(Du(x)) dx (Q is an isometry and Xt(G(x)) = psi(G(x)) (0, phi(x))) = integral over ball 0 r of J(Du(x)) dx, because psi(G(x)) = 1 where phi(x) is nonzero and the integrand vanishes off tsupport phi, contained in Bo^n_r(0), contained in D_s. (h is continuous on U, so this integrand is continuous with compact support.) 8. Conclusion. The generalized mean curvature identity integral of divM X dmu = - integral of dmu, with steps 6 and 7, gives for every such phi: integral over ball 0 r of fderiv J (fderiv u x) (fderiv phi x) dx = - integral over ball 0 r of J(fderiv u x) * dx. Together with steps 1 and 2 this proves the statement (with the r of step 2, 0 < r <= R).
proof_key_steps: O is open and F is locally C^{q,alpha} by invariance under affine isometries
choose r with |(x, u(x))| < s for |x| < r
the tangent planes of V equal the graph's tangent planes mu-a.e. (dohr_graph_tangent_planes)
vertical test field X = Q^{-1} psi (0, phi o pi) composed with T
trace formula J(Du) div_M X = DJ(Du)[Dphi] (Jacobi's formula)
area formula on both sides of the first variation identity

audit.reason: Affine-isometry transport proves the exact local Hölder assertion. The compactly supported vertical field is admissible, and the declared tangent-plane dependency justifies its tangential divergence. Jacobi's formula and the area formula produce the stated derivative of J and the correct negative curvature integral. The inline matrix construction was independently checked.
